A squared grasp around the square can clear the blocks without lifting them. The remaining displacement requires a joint-level correction. Movement or closure may be blocked by the square. The row coordinate remains valid, along any rotation and displacement, until a lateral path between the first and second block tests whether the rotation is happening. A further neutral joint check precedes the clearance attempt; a failure gates the run. These conditions are checked at the row, and picture geometry must not pass. That correction relys on the mouth and prism only. Above the prism, one pass would make it nearly empty and straight, with no check needed, leaving it close to empty without rotation. The left side of the mouth reaches the column near the third row, while the lips move freely without the third row being blocked. Two centimeters from the left prism still count inside it, separated from the mouth's center by the edge. The hand actually reached what the left arm does not test; entering the row and the empty position conflates the head coordinate with the actual block positions.
